evals.name: check-is-default-and-read-only
evals.expected_output: Routes to check (the default action): probes Bash 5.0+, jq presence, each guard's effective toggle, the cli-flag-verify scan surface, the block-dangerous-git allowlist, and hook registration. Reports a PASS/FAIL/INFO table with one remediation line per FAIL. Edits nothing — every tunable is native userConfig.
expectations: Routes to the check action when no argument is given
Reports PASS/FAIL/INFO for Bash, jq, and per-guard toggles rather than inventing configuration
Does not write settings, pluginConfigs, or any consumer-project file during check

evals.name: apply-points-only-never-writes
evals.expected_output: Runs check first, then for each FAIL points at the resolution: platform install guidance for missing jq or old Bash, and /plugin configure guardrails (or the documented headless uninstall/reinstall --config sequence) for toggle or scalar changes. Installs nothing and writes nothing — apply is pure guidance.
expectations: Points at /plugin configure or the documented headless reconfigure sequence for toggle changes
Never installs system packages and never writes user settings or pluginConfigs

evals.name: disabled-guards-downgrade-prereq-failures
evals.prompt:
/guardrails:setup check

Every guard toggle is disabled on this machine and jq is missing.
evals.expected_output: When every guard's toggle is disabled, the missing-jq prerequisite downgrades from FAIL to INFO — a deliberately disabled plugin is not broken. Reports the probes informationally and notes that re-enabling restores the FAIL semantics.
expectations: Treats missing jq as INFO rather than FAIL when every guard toggle is disabled
Notes that re-enabling a guard restores the FAIL semantics for prerequisites
Does not claim the plugin is broken solely because jq is absent while all guards are off

evals.name: install-commit-msg-is-opt-in-only
evals.expected_output: Bare apply does not install the commit-msg hook. The DEPTH-layer commit-msg convention hook installs only when the explicit `apply install-commit-msg` argument is given; it writes only the operator's personal .git/hooks/ lane and never a committed team hooksPath.
expectations: Does not install a commit-msg hook from bare apply
States that install-commit-msg is the opt-in argument that installs the personal hook
Does not configure core.hooksPath or write a tracked team hooks directory from this skill
